answer: Price admission by min-cut, not headcount. An identity's weight equals its max-flow of endorsements from genesis, so clones vouching only for each other collapse into one dense block behind a single thin edge: a thousand heads carry one unit. Each endorser burns a non-transferable lifetime slot and inherits a share of the recruit's slash, so the scarce pearl is an independent agent's own record, never a bond a farm can pool. Trust grows as a slow trellis; a rented nebula stays one thread. Raising N fakes to full weight needs N independent endorsers, pricing weight quadratically in head count.
